title: Graphing Linear Functions: Intercepts, Zeros and Slope
seo_title: Algebra I Graphing Linear Functions Worksheets (TEKS A.3C)
standard_text: A.3C graph linear functions on the coordinate plane and identify key features, including x-intercept, y-intercept, zeros, and slope, in mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Algebra I worksheets for Texas TEKS A.3C: graph linear functions, find x- and y-intercepts and zeros, read slope and intercept in context. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Start at the y-intercept, then move by the slope.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In y = mx + b, start at the y-intercept (0, b) and move by the slope m.
  • The x-intercept is where y = 0. It is also the zero of the function.
  • For Ax + By = C, put x = 0 to find the y-intercept and y = 0 to find the x-intercept.

Examples

Example

3x + 2y = 12

x = 0: y = 6

y = 0: x = 4

Answer: intercepts (0, 6) and (4, 0); zero 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Mixing up the interceptsThe x-intercept has y = 0.
Plotting the slope as the interceptStart at b, then use m.
Forgetting the zeroThe zero is the x-intercept.

items.q: Write −2x + 4y = −12 in slope-intercept form.
items.e: Add 2x to both sides, then divide every term by 4: y = 12x − 3.

items.q: Find the x- and y-intercepts of 5x − 4y = 40.
items.e: Let y = 0: 5x = 40, so x = 8. Let x = 0: −4y = 40, so y = −10. x-intercept 8, y-intercept −10.

items.q: Find the x- and y-intercepts of 2x + 3y = 6.
items.e: Let y = 0: 2x = 6, so x = 3. Let x = 0: 3y = 6, so y = 2. x-intercept 3, y-intercept 2.

items.q: Write 6x + 2y = 6 in slope-intercept form.
items.e: Subtract 6x from both sides, then divide every term by 2: y = −3x + 3.

items.q: Write y = 12x + 1 in standard form Ax + By = C with integer coefficients and A > 0.
items.e: Multiply every term by 2 to clear the fraction, move the x-term to the left and make the x-coefficient positive: x − 2y = −2.

items.q: Write 3x + 4y = −12 in slope-intercept form.

items.q: Find the x- and y-intercepts of 4x − 2y = 8.

sets.title: What the slope and intercept mean

items.q: In y = 25x + 100, what does 25 mean? (x = months, y = dollars saved)
items.e: The slope is the change for each month: $25 saved each month.

items.q: For y = 4x + 10, what is y when x = 6?
In y = 25x + 100, what does 100 mean? (x = months, y = dollars saved)
items.e: The y-intercept is the value when x = 0: $100 at the start.

items.q: For y = −2x + 50, what is y when x = 15?
In y = −3x + 60, what does −3 mean? (x = minutes, y = liters of water)
items.e: A negative slope is a decrease: 3 liters drain each minute.

items.q: For y = 12x + 3, what is y when x = 8?
items.e: 12 × 8 + 3 = 7.

items.q: In y = −3x + 60, what does 60 mean? (x = minutes, y = liters of water)
items.e: At x = 0 there are 60 liters at the start.

items.q: For y = 3x − 5, what is x when y = 16?
In y = 0.5x + 2, what does 0.5 mean? (x = miles, y = taxi cost in dollars)
items.e: The slope is the cost for each mile: $0.50 per mile.

items.q: For y = −5x + 40, what is x when y = 0?
In y = 8x, what is the initial value? (x = hours, y = dollars earned)
items.e: y = 8x + 0, so the initial value is $0 (no money at the start).

items.q: For y = 6x + 12, what is x when y = 48?
In y = 12x + 5, when x goes up by 2, how much does y go up?
items.e: Each step of 1 adds 12, so 2 steps add 12 × 2 = 24.

items.q: For y = 2x + 7, what is y when x = 9?
In y = −4x + 9, what is y when x = 0?
For y = −x + 20, what is x when y = 8?
In y = 3x − 7, where does the line cross the y-axis?
items.e: The y-intercept is b = −7, the point (0, −7).

items.q: For y = 10x, what is y when x = 7?
In y = 15x + 30, a gym: x = classes, y = total cost. What is the cost for 4 classes?
For y = 1 12x − 1, what is x when y = 11?
items.e: Solve 11 = 1 12x − 1: 1 12x = 12, so x = 8.

items.q: Which describes the graph of height over time?
c: It goes up, stays the same, then goes down
It goes down, stays the same, then goes up
It stays the same the whole time
It goes up the whole time
items.e: Read from left to right. It goes up, stays the same, then goes down. The answer is it goes up, stays the same, then goes down.

items.q: A function is increasing. What happens to y as x gets bigger?
items.e: Increasing means y gets bigger as x gets bigger.

items.q: Which describes the graph of water over time?
c: It stays the same, then goes down
It goes up, then stays the same
It goes down, then stays the same
It goes down the whole time
items.e: Read from left to right. It goes down, then stays the same. The answer is it goes down, then stays the same.

items.q: On a graph of distance over time, what does a flat part mean?
items.e: Distance does not change, so the person is not moving.

items.q: Which describes the graph of distance over time?
c: It goes up the whole time at the same speed
It goes up, then down, then up
It goes up, stays the same, then goes up again
items.e: Read from left to right. It goes up, stays the same, then goes up again. The answer is it goes up, stays the same, then goes up again.

items.q: A linear function has slope −2. Is it increasing or decreasing?
items.e: A negative slope means y goes down as x goes up: decreasing.

items.q: Mia walks to school, stops to talk to a friend, then runs the rest of the way. Which graph shape fits distance from home?
c: Up, flat, then up more steeply
items.e: Walking: going up. Stopping: flat. Running: going up faster (steeper). Up, flat, then up more steeply.

items.q: On a graph of distance from home over time, what does a part going down mean?
items.e: Distance from home gets smaller: going back toward home.

items.q: Which describes the graph of speed over time?
c: It stays the same the whole time
items.e: Read from left to right. It stays the same the whole time. The answer is it stays the same the whole time.

items.q: A linear function has slope 0. What does its graph look like?
items.e: Slope 0 means y never changes: a horizontal line.

items.q: A bath fills with water, Ben takes a bath, then the water drains out. Which shape fits the water level?
items.e: Filling: up. Bath: flat. Draining: down. Up, flat, then down.

items.q: Which part of a distance–time graph shows the fastest speed?
items.e: Steeper means more distance in the same time: the steepest part.

items.q: Which describes the graph of temperature over time?
c: It goes up the whole time
It goes down, goes up, then goes down
It goes down the whole time
It goes up, goes down, then goes up
items.e: Read from left to right. It goes down, goes up, then goes down. The answer is it goes down, goes up, then goes down.

items.q: The height of a ball thrown up goes up, then comes down. Is height a linear function of time?
items.e: It rises then falls along a curve: no, it is nonlinear.

items.q: A car speeds up, drives at a steady speed, then slows to a stop. Which shape fits its speed?
items.e: Speeding up: up. Steady: flat. Stopping: down to 0. Up, flat, then down to 0.

items.q: A runner keeps the same speed for the whole race. Is distance a linear function of time?
items.e: The same speed means the same change each second: yes, it is linear.

items.q: A balloon is let go and rises at a steady rate. Which shape fits its height?
items.e: A steady rise is a straight line going up. A straight line going up.

items.q: In which interval is the function increasing: it goes from 2 to 8 between x = 0 and x = 3, then from 8 to 1 between x = 3 and x = 6?
items.e: y goes up from 2 to 8 only from x = 0 to x = 3.

items.q: A phone battery drains at a steady rate while you watch a video. Which shape fits the battery level?
items.e: A steady drain is a straight line going down: a straight line going down.

items.q: A graph of savings goes up by the same amount each week. What kind of function is it?
items.e: The same increase each week: linear and increasing.
